examples.en: On the weekend I did all the small household chores at once.
There are so many small jobs since this morning that I'm in a whirl.

examples.ko: 잔일은 제가 할 테니 앉아서 쉬세요.
examples.en: I'll do the small jobs, so please sit and rest.

examples.ko: 신입 사원은 잔일도 열심히 해야 해요.
examples.en: New employees have to work hard even on the small jobs.
I'm tired from being bogged down in odd jobs all day.

examples.ko: 큰일 하기 전에 잔일부터 끝내 두세요.
examples.en: Before the big task, finish the small jobs first.

explain: '큰일'의 반대로, 중요하지 않지만 자꾸 생기는 자질구레한 일을 말해요. '허드렛일'과 비슷하게 쓸 수 있고, 집안일이나 회사의 심부름 같은 일에 많이 써요.
explain_en: As the opposite of '큰일' (a big matter), it means trivial tasks that keep popping up. It can be used much like '허드렛일', and is common for household chores or errand-like work at the office.

examples.ko: 감독이 선수들과 함께 팀을 재정비하고 있어요.
examples.en: The coach is rebuilding the team together with the players.
After exams are over, I rework my study plan.
They decided to refurbish and reorganize the old market.
I took a short break and got myself back in order.

examples.ko: 회사는 조직을 재정비한 뒤에 새 사업을 시작해요.
examples.en: The company restructures its organization and then starts a new business.
The roads are jammed while the road is being redone.

explain: 팀, 조직, 계획, 마음가짐처럼 흐트러진 것을 다시 갖추는 느낌으로 써요. 고장 난 물건을 수리할 때는 그냥 '고치다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It gives the feeling of putting something that has gotten loose, such as a team, organization, plan or state of mind, back in shape. For repairing a broken object, people just say '고치다'.

examples.ko: 남편이 다음 달에 부산으로 전근을 가요.
examples.en: My husband is transferring to Busan next month.

examples.ko: 전근 때문에 아이들 학교를 옮겨야 해요.
examples.en: Because of the transfer, we have to move the kids' school.
My colleagues were sad when they heard the news of my transfer.

examples.ko: 지방 전근이 결정돼서 이사 준비를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: My transfer to the provinces was decided, so I'm preparing to move.

examples.ko: 전근은 보통 인사 발표 때 결정돼요.
examples.en: Transfers are usually decided when personnel announcements are made.

examples.ko: 전근 가서 새 동네에 적응하는 중이에요.
examples.en: I transferred and am getting used to a new neighborhood.

explain: 같은 회사나 기관 안에서 다른 지역이나 근무지로 옮기는 일이에요. 회사를 바꾸는 '이직'과 달라요. '전근 가다/전근을 가다'로 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It means moving to a different region or workplace within the same company or organization. It differs from '이직', which means changing employers. It is commonly said as '전근 가다' or '전근을 가다'.

en: to be entirely responsible for; to pay for something alone

examples.en: Mr. Kim is solely in charge of counseling new students.
Our team took sole charge of that work.
It is hard to handle childcare all by yourself.

examples.ko: 병원에는 환자 안내를 전담하는 직원이 있어요.
examples.en: The hospital has staff dedicated to guiding patients.

examples.ko: 그 프로젝트는 우리 부서가 전담할 거예요.
examples.en: Our department will handle that project alone.

examples.ko: 번역을 전담해 줄 사람을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for someone to handle the translation exclusively.

explain: 한 사람이나 한 부서가 어떤 일을 혼자 도맡을 때 써요. '담당하다'는 그 일을 맡는다는 점만 말하고, '전담하다'는 다른 사람은 하지 않고 그 사람만 한다는 느낌이 더해져요. '업무를 전담하다', '전담 부서'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Use it when one person or one department handles a task alone. 담당하다 only says someone is in charge, while 전담하다 adds that nobody else does it. It appears as '업무를 전담하다' and '전담 부서'.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 모든 고객 정보를 전산화했어요.
examples.en: Our company digitized all of its customer information.

examples.ko: 도서관에서 오래된 책 목록을 전산화하고 있어요.
examples.en: The library is digitizing its old book list.

examples.ko: 병원이 진료 기록을 전산화하면 훨씬 편해요.
examples.en: If a hospital digitizes its medical records, it's much more convenient.

examples.ko: 종이 장부를 전산화하려고 새 프로그램을 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a new program to digitize the paper ledger.

examples.ko: 시청에서는 민원 서류를 먼저 전산화할 거예요.
examples.en: The city hall will digitize the civil service documents first.
Even small shops need to digitize their inventory.

explain: 종이나 사람 손으로 하던 일을 컴퓨터로 처리하게 바꾼다는 느낌이라 사무·행정 이야기에서 써요. 보통 자료, 기록, 업무 같은 말이 목적어로 오고, '전산화되다'라는 형태도 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It means changing work done on paper or by hand into computer processing, so it is used in office and administrative talk. Objects are usually things like data, records or tasks, and the form '전산화되다' (be digitized) also appears often.

examples.en: This year I'll concentrate on studying English.
This company focuses its efforts on developing new products.
I'm putting my main effort into exercise for my health.
Before the exam, I focused on review.
Which field are you focusing on these days?

examples.ko: 한 가지에만 주력하면 다른 일을 놓칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you focus on just one thing, you may miss other things.

explain: '주력하다'는 '~에 주력하다'로 써서 여러 일 중에 가장 큰 힘을 쏟는 곳을 말해요. '집중하다'는 정신을 한곳에 모으는 느낌이고, '주력하다'는 회사, 팀, 계획의 중심 방향을 말할 때 잘 어울려요. '주력 상품', '주력 분야'처럼 명사로도 써요.
explain_en: 주력하다 is used as '~에 주력하다' to name where you pour the most effort among many tasks. 집중하다 is more about gathering your attention on one spot, while 주력하다 fits the main direction of a company, team, or plan. It also works as a noun-modifier in 주력 상품 (flagship product) and 주력 분야 (main field).

examples.ko: 회사에서 직원 세 명을 행사에 차출했어요.
examples.en: The company pulled three employees for the event.

examples.ko: 구단은 선수를 대표팀에 차출하지 않기로 했어요.
examples.en: The club decided not to release the player to the national team.

examples.ko: 급한 일이 생겨서 다른 부서 사람들을 차출해야 해요.
examples.en: Something urgent came up, so we have to pull people from other departments.

examples.ko: 대표팀이 선수들을 차출하면 시즌 경기가 힘들어져요.
examples.en: If the national team calls up the players, the season games get harder.

examples.ko: 시청에서 공무원을 차출해서 행사를 돕게 했어요.
examples.en: City Hall pulled civil servants to help with the event.
The coach said he would pull me for the team.

explain: 'A를 B에 차출하다'처럼 사람을 목적어로 써요. '뽑다'보다 원래 있던 자리에서 빼 와서 쓴다는 느낌이 강하고, 시키는 쪽의 결정이 중심이에요. 스포츠 기사나 회사 이야기에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It takes a person as the object, as in 'A를 B에 차출하다'. It feels more like pulling someone out of their original place than simply choosing them with '뽑다', and the decision lies with the one giving the order. You can see it in sports articles and workplace talk.

examples.ko: 시청은 다음 달에 새 도서관을 착공할 예정이에요.
examples.en: The city hall plans to break ground on a new library next month.

examples.ko: 아파트를 착공하고 나서 이 년 만에 완성했어요.
examples.en: They finished the apartment building two years after starting construction.

examples.ko: 공사를 착공하려면 허가를 먼저 받아야 해요.
examples.en: To begin construction, you must get a permit first.
Residents were glad at the news that construction on the bridge would begin.
The day construction starts was pushed back because of rain.

examples.ko: 지난해에 착공한 지하철 노선이 곧 완성돼요.
examples.en: The subway line begun last year will soon be complete.

explain: 건물, 도로, 다리처럼 큰 공사를 시작할 때만 써요. 반대말은 '준공하다'(공사를 마치다)예요. 집 청소나 작은 수리를 시작할 때는 쓰지 않고 '시작하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used only when a big construction project such as a building, road or bridge begins. Its opposite is 준공하다 (to complete construction). For small jobs like cleaning or minor repairs, just say 시작하다.

en: to begin work on; to set about (a task or project)

examples.en: The company embarked on a new business.
Construction is scheduled to start next week.
The police immediately began their investigation.
Once the materials are gathered, we'll get started on the work.

examples.ko: 연구에 착수하기 전에 계획을 세워야 해요.
examples.en: You need to make a plan before starting the research.
Once the team members got to work, the mood improved.

explain: 착수하다는 일이나 공사, 수사처럼 비교적 큰 일을 실제로 시작할 때 써요. '시작하다'보다 격식 있고 '일에 손을 대다'는 느낌이에요. '수사에 착수하다', '공사에 착수하다'처럼 굳은 짝이 많아요.
explain_en: 착수하다 is used when actually starting a fairly large task, such as a project, construction, or an investigation. It is more formal than '시작하다' and feels like putting your hand to the work. It has set pairs like '수사에 착수하다' and '공사에 착수하다'.

p.n: The replacement is the general word, less formal and not specific to tasks.

examples.en: The manager made the new employee attend the meeting.
The school has students attend the event.
Please don't force the child to attend.
The CEO wants to have all the team members attend.
Many companies have employees attend training.
I asked whether we could have guests attend.

explain: '참석하다'는 본인이 가는 것이고, '참석시키다'는 다른 사람을 가게 하는 거예요. 회사와 학교처럼 위에서 정하는 상황에서 쓰고, 친구 사이에서는 잘 안 써요. 가볍게는 '오게 하다', '보내다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: 참석하다 is going yourself, while 참석시키다 is getting someone else to go. It fits company or school settings where someone in charge decides, and rarely appears between friends. Casually, people say 오게 하다 or 보내다.

examples.en: The company put a lot of money into the new business.
The coach sends in a new player in the second half.

examples.ko: 사람을 더 투입하면 일이 빨리 끝나요.
examples.en: If we put in more people, the work finishes faster.

examples.ko: 소방대가 불을 끄려고 헬기를 투입할 거래요.
examples.en: I hear the fire department will send in a helicopter to put out the fire.
Check before you put the materials into the machine.

examples.ko: 시간을 많이 투입한 만큼 결과가 좋아요.
examples.en: The result is good in proportion to the time put in.

explain: 돈, 사람, 시간, 장비처럼 일에 필요한 것을 넣을 때 써요. '넣다'보다 딱딱하고 계획적인 느낌이에요. '인력을 투입하다', '예산을 투입하다'처럼 같이 쓰는 말이 거의 정해져 있어요.
explain_en: Use it for putting in what a job needs: money, people, time, equipment. It is stiffer and more planned than '넣다'. Common pairs are '인력을 투입하다' and '예산을 투입하다'.
